result.question: I'm worried the paper insulation in Transformer 1 at MAIN may be involved. Pull co and co2 for every sample in the available window and work out the CO2/CO ratio for each sample. Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. If co2 has no data at all, report the co trend alongside oxygen instead and say that the ratio test couldn't be done.
result.answer:
All five samples for Transformer 1 at MAIN are flagged, but for general cellulose ageing, not for paper involved in a fault. Every CO2/CO ratio is above 10 (between 38.6 and 43.3), and none is below 3.

**Window:** 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, one sample per day. Both co and co2 are present in every sample, so no ratios were skipped and the oxygen fallback wasn't needed.

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO2 (ppm) | CO2/CO | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.00 | >10: general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.33 | >10: general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.57 | >10: general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.15 | >10: general cellulose ageing |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.88 | >10: general cellulose ageing |

**Statistics over the window:**
| Sensor | Min | Max | Mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| CO | 30 | 35 | 32.4 |
| CO2 | 1300 | 1350 | 1331.8 |

**Trend:** Across the samples the ratio is essentially flat, with a very slight downward drift. A least-squares fit gives a slope of about −0.34 per day, and the ratio went from 42.00 on the first day to 41.88 on the last. The lowest point, 38.57 on 01-17, came from a small rise in CO to 35 ppm and was not sustained. With only 5 samples, this change is within normal day-to-day variation.

**What this means:** CO is low and stable at about 30–35 ppm, and the ratio is nowhere near 3. The data doesn't suggest the paper insulation is involved in an active fault. The consistently high ratio (about 40) points to slow, general cellulose ageing, possibly with some CO2 coming from oil oxidation or taken up from the air. Keep monitoring the ratio, and take a sharp fall toward 3 as the warning sign.
